content.Text:
Here’s what I found (checked today, April 26, 2026):

**(a) Local run feasibility**
- DeepSeek‑V4‑Pro is released as open weights (1.6T total params, 49B active, 1M context) on Hugging Face, and the model card explicitly includes a “How to Run Locally” section. ([huggingface.co](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Pro))  
- The official local workflow requires converting HF weights and then running distributed inference with `torchrun`, using model parallelism (example shows `MP=8`), plus optional FP8/FP4 handling in config. That means local inference is **feasible**, but **practically requires multi‑GPU, distributed setup** and significant resources. ([huggingface.co](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Pro/blob/main/inference/README.md))  
- The model card recommends `temperature=1.0, top_p=1.0`, and for “Think Max” it recommends a **context window ≥384K tokens**, which implies large KV cache and even more memory pressure. ([huggingface.co](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Pro))  
- On the Unsloth HF page, the model is **not deployed by any HF Inference Provider**, so you cannot “one‑click” run it via HF inference; you need your own hardware or a third‑party host. ([huggingface.co](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Pro))

**Conclusion:** Local run is possible, but only in a serious multi‑GPU environment with distributed inference and weight conversion.

**(b) OpenRouter compatibility**
- OpenRouter lists **`deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`** as an available model with 1,048,576 context and a release date of **April 24, 2026**, which confirms compatibility via OpenRouter’s API. ([openrouter.ai](https://openrouter.ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro))  
- The OpenRouter DeepSeek catalog also explicitly includes DeepSeek V4 Pro. ([openrouter.ai](https://openrouter.ai/deepseek))
If you want, tell me your hardware (GPUs + VRAM) and I’ll sanity‑check whether local inference is realistic for you.
